questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, why are short-acting drugs chosen?
questions.answer: For early neurological assessment

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia positioning, which way should the head be turned?
Which line is often used to monitor blood pressure in neuroanaesthesia?
What level of postoperative care is common after neurosurgery?
In neuroanaesthesia, what is probably one of the most important ways to prevent brain injury?
questions.answer: Blood pressure control

questions.stem: What cerebral perfusion pressure should neuroanaesthesia aim for?
With an ICP monitor in place, neuroanaesthesia aims for a CPP of ____.
In neuroanaesthesia, how close should blood pressure stay to baseline?
In neuroanaesthesia, what determines the blood pressure target?
questions.answer: The pathology

questions.stem: In ischaemic stroke with thrombolysis contraindicated, what SBP limit applies?
In ischaemic stroke given thrombolysis, what SBP limit applies?
In subarachnoid haemorrhage, what SBP limit applies until the aneurysm is secured?
For intracerebral haemorrhage other than SAH, what SBP target applies?
Which lines are used to monitor and control blood pressure in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: Arterial line, with or without a central venous catheter

questions.stem: What is the IV dose of labetalol for blood pressure control in neuroanaesthesia?
What is the IV dose of nicardipine for blood pressure control in neuroanaesthesia?
For neuroprotection in neuroanaesthesia, which physiological states should be maintained?
questions.answer: Normotension, normoxia, normocarbia, normothermia and normoglycaemia

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, when is seizure prophylaxis given?
options: Only after a seizure has occurred
Routinely, before the dura is opened

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, when should brain relaxation be achieved?
questions.answer: Before the dura is opened

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, how far should the head be raised to help venous drainage?
For brain relaxation in neuroanaesthesia, what must be adequate, and what should be avoided on emergence?
questions.answer: Anaesthetic depth, analgesia and paralysis; avoid agitation on emergence

questions.stem: What PaCO2 is targeted during neuroanaesthesia surgery?
What core temperature is targeted for normothermia in neuroanaesthesia?
In neuroanaesthesia, what PEEP ceiling is advised, and why?
questions.answer: PEEP at or below 10 cm H2O: higher levels impair venous drainage and raise ICP

questions.stem: How quickly should mannitol be given in neuroanaesthesia?
What adverse effect can mannitol cause in neuroanaesthesia?
Which diuretic replaces mannitol or hypertonic saline in cardiac disease in neuroanaesthesia?
Why are patients with cardiac disease given furosemide instead of mannitol or hypertonic saline?
questions.answer: They may not tolerate a volume load

questions.stem: What dexamethasone dose is given for tumours in neuroanaesthesia, if indicated?
What MAC range is kept for isoflurane or sevoflurane in neuroanaesthesia?
Why must volatile anaesthetic concentration stay below 1 MAC in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: To avoid raising ICP

questions.stem: Which anaesthetic technique is often preferred for intracranial surgery?
Why is propofol TIVA thought to suit intracranial surgery?
questions.answer: It keeps cerebral flow-metabolism coupling and CO2 reactivity intact

questions.stem: Which drug class is the gold standard for cerebral protection in neuroanaesthesia?
What does etomidate progressively do to cerebral metabolism in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: Lowers it to an isoelectric EEG

questions.stem: Why are benzodiazepines not used for cerebral protection in neuroanaesthesia?
options: They cannot fully suppress the EEG
They strongly raise cerebral blood flow
They are too short acting to use

questions.stem: Which opioid should be avoided in neuroanaesthesia?
In neuroanaesthesia, which relaxant class do most prefer over suxamethonium?
questions.answer: A non-depolarising NMBD

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, why is nitrous oxide a concern for intracranial pressure?
options: Cerebral vasoconstriction, lowering CBF and ICP
Cerebral vasodilation, raising CBF and ICP
Reduced cerebral blood flow with no ICP change

questions.stem: What does nitrous oxide do to air-filled spaces, and what risk does that carry?
questions.answer: Expands air: venous air embolism, pneumocephalus

questions.stem: What does ketamine do to intracranial pressure in neuroanaesthesia?
What emergence problem may ketamine cause in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: Emergence delirium

questions.stem: What neurological drawback does morphine have after neurosurgery?
questions.answer: Hampers postoperative neurological monitoring

questions.stem: What respiratory effect does morphine have in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: Respiratory depression

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, how should benzodiazepines be used, and why?
questions.answer: Sparingly, to allow rapid emergence and neurological assessment

questions.stem: Which is the fluid of choice in neuroanaesthesia?
Which fluid should be avoided in neuroanaesthesia because it worsens cerebral oedema?
Which fluid type should be avoided in neuroanaesthesia because it worsens ischaemia and oedema?
Why is fluid restriction no longer used for raised ICP in neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: Only moderately effective; causes hypotension and cerebral and renal hypoperfusion

questions.stem: Which neurocritical care monitors may patients arrive with for neuroanaesthesia?
questions.answer: External ventricular drain (EVD), SjVO2 catheter, brain tissue oxygen probe

questions.stem: In neuroanaesthesia, what should happen to neurocritical care monitors where possible?
questions.answer: Continue them through the perioperative period
